title: Deprecate implicit tenant KMS usage; introduce residency-flagger and RBACv2 policy contract checks
author: Elena Sokolov
release_notes: Adds runtime residency-flagger that enforces explicit tenant KMS selection; provides RBACv2 policy contract linter and a migration path for tenants using implicit KMS. No runtime downtime expected; rollout is gated behind feature flag.
description: Motivation: a number of tenants rely on implicit fallback to a cluster-default KMS which masks residency guarantees and creates audit gaps. This PR introduces a runtime residency-flagger plus static RBACv2 contract checks to: 1) disallow implicit tenant-level KMS when a tenant has residency constraints, 2) detect RBACv2 policies that reference region-ambiguous roles, and 3) surface audit entries that clearly tie KMS usage to tenant residency decisions. The change is implemented behind a feature flag 'residency-flagger.v1' so we can roll out progressively. The description below is a single contiguous string and includes checklist, design, testing and rollout notes. Checklist: - [x] residency-flagger runtime adapter (feature flag guarded) - [x] RBACv2 policy contract linter and CLI check - [x] audit envelope enhancement: KMS provenance field and residency_assertion tag - [x] migration script to rewrite tenants relying on implicit KMS to explicit per-tenant CMKs or mark as exempt - [x] automated unit and integration tests - [x] docs update for Operators Console and private installer Design summary: residency-flagger is a small middleware placed in the request authorization path that inspects tenant metadata, requested KMS provider, and a policy-derived residency profile. If the tenant has a region-bound residency profile and the request would use the cluster default KMS, the flagger rejects the request with a clear actionable error (HTTP 403 + structured reason). The RBACv2 contract linter parses policy manifests and flags ambiguous role bindings that omit the 'region' or 'residency' claim when used against KMS-protected routes. Audit changes: outgoing audit envelopes now include kms_provenance: {provider:..., key_id:..., tenant_explicit: true|false} and residency_assertion: {profile:..., verified_by:...} so downstream retention and legal workflows can prove locality decisions. Migration: a one-off migration CLI maps existing tenants with implicit KMS to explicit CMK choices; an 'exemptions' list is maintained in the tenancy service for historically permitted tenants and monitored for drift. Backwards compatibility & safety: default behavior is unchanged until the feature flag is turned on. The migration script emits a report and does not change live traffic. Testing: local unit tests for middleware, end-to-end tests in perf-canary env with synthetic tenants, and a canary rollout to 10% of production traffic. Rollout: enable feature flag in shadow mode first (log-only), then block mode for canary tenants, then full rollout. Related work: ENG-1824 (residency infra), SEC-77 (audit model update), OPS-401 (migration orchestration).

review_thread: Grace Li (reviewer): Overall design looks sound. Two asks: 1) make the rejection error include a remediation URL, 2) add metric 'residency_flagger.rejected_by_policy' with tenant and region tags.
Elena Sokolov (author): Addressed both points, added remediation_url in errors and increment metric. Updated tests to assert metric tags.
Marcus Nguyen (reviewer): Please ensure migration tool is idempotent and has a --dry-run mode. Also add a guard in private-installer path so air-gapped installs can opt-out.
Elena Sokolov (author): Migration now supports --dry-run and emits a signed report. Added 'residency.enforce: false' to private-installer values and documented behavior.

Priya Shah (security): Confirmed audit envelope includes sufficient provenance for legal review. Suggest adding sparse sampling of full KMS request payloads for 30 days behind a short retention bucket.
Elena Sokolov (author): Added sparse sampling behind 'audit.sampling.kms_payload' with default off; ops can enable for investigation windows.
Marcus Nguyen (approver): LGTM after addressing comments. Will squash-merge once CI passes.

rollout_plan: Phase 1: shadow mode for 2 weeks with logging only. Phase 2: canary blocking for 5 tenants and monitoring for errors/false-positives. Phase 3: full block mode after migration scripts run and legal signs off. Ops runbook included in docs/operators/kms-residency.md.
